command: copilot (interactive TUI, driven under a pty), prompted to delegate with its `task` tool
note: First real bytes through copilot's Task path — claimed by NAME (`task`), deliberately not by a `subagent_type` key, so a model-authored arg cannot spoof an ordinary tool into a delegation and drain active_tasks. Flat here, unlike the conformance tree: copilot keys on the transcript's PARENT DIR, and this module hands the decoder that logical path explicitly rather than reproducing the directory. Redacted: home path rewritten to /Users/dev; the owner column of a captured `ls -la`. The bytes are otherwise verbatim. Redacted: the recorder's own MCP server / skill inventory (tool NAMES only, no credentials) to generic placeholders — a public repo and an immutable crates.io tarball are the wrong home for one machine's tooling roster, and no decoder reads those fields. Redacted: the recorder's installed plugin roster — skill and agent names, their descriptions, and the install paths that give the names back — to `example-skill-N` / `example-plugin-N:example-agent` placeholders, collapsed to three entries because the COUNT is this machine's inventory size too. Each CLI's own bundled set is kept, told apart mechanically rather than by a name list: a `:` in a claude-code agent type means plugin-provided, copilot tags `<location>builtin</location>`, codex roots its own at `r2/` or `.codex/skills/.system/`. No decoder reads any of these fields and every conformance golden is byte-identical.
